overview: This Senate resolution marks the fourth anniversary of the mass shooting at the Fourth of July parade in Highland Park, Illinois, on July 4, 2022, in which a gunman killed seven people and injured 48. It names and remembers each of the seven victims and offers condolences to their families and support to those injured. It thanks the many police, fire, medical and emergency workers who responded, and expresses solidarity with victims of gun violence across the country. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on July 15, 2026.
for: Supporters say it honors the victims, comforts their families and recognizes the first responders and medical workers who helped.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or spending.
